name: 鏡頭01開始
body:
1976: a double canoe left Hawaiʻi with
no compass, no sextant, no map.
notes: EN48 p2 鏡頭01開始 — 4 s — 1976: a double canoe left Hawaiʻi with no compass, no sextant, no map.

name: 鏡頭01結束＝鏡頭02開始
body:
1976: a double canoe left Hawaiʻi with
no compass, no sextant, no map.
notes: EN48 p3 鏡頭01結束＝鏡頭02開始 — 4 s — 1976: a double canoe left Hawaiʻi with no compass, no sextant, no map.

name: 鏡頭02結束
body:
Its name, Hōkūleʻa, is Arcturus — “star
of gladness.”
plan: E03; labels 大角星／角宿一 → Arcturus／Spica (Hōkūleʻa, Hikianalia stay)
notes: EN48 p4 鏡頭02結束 — 4 s — Its name, Hōkūleʻa, is Arcturus — “star of gladness.”

notes: EN48 p5 鏡頭02-概念圖1 — 3 s — 34 days to Tahiti

name: 鏡頭02-概念圖收＝鏡頭03開始
headline: The navigator: Mau Piailug
body:
From Satawal, Micronesia. By then,
Hawaiʻi’s deep-sea wayfinding was long
lost.
plan: diagram fades; E05; labels as page 4; then straight to 11 (pages 8–10, the Chinese star-compass diagram, removed)
notes: EN48 p7 鏡頭02-概念圖收＝鏡頭03開始 — 5 s — The navigator: Mau Piailug From Satawal, Micronesia. By then, Hawaiʻi’s deep-sea wayfinding was long lost.

name: 鏡頭04-概念圖收＝鏡頭05開始
headline: Four star lines
body:
His student Nainoa Thompson split the
sky into four north-south star lines.
plan: E06; label 脊椎骨 → the backbone (Ka Iwikuamoʻo stays)
notes: EN48 p11 鏡頭04-概念圖收＝鏡頭05開始 — 6 s — Four star lines His student Nainoa Thompson split the sky into four north-south star lines.

name: 鏡頭05結束＝鏡頭06開始
body:
Not an ancient chart — a modern
navigator’s notes for memorising the
sky.
plan: E07; label 南十字 → Southern Cross (Hānaiakamalama stays)
notes: EN48 p12 鏡頭05結束＝鏡頭06開始 — 5 s — Not an ancient chart — a modern navigator’s notes for memorising the sky.

name: 鏡頭06結束
headline: Ka Iwikuamoʻo: the backbone
body:
From the Southern Cross, past Hōkūleʻa,
up to Hōkūpaʻa, the North Star.
plan: E08; label 北極星 → North Star (Hōkūpaʻa stays)
notes: EN48 p13 鏡頭06結束 — 6 s — Ka Iwikuamoʻo: the backbone From the Southern Cross, past Hōkūleʻa, up to Hōkūpaʻa, the North Star.

name: 長圖轉北盤1＝鏡頭07開始
headline: Four spokes, four seasons
body:
Winter: Makaliʻi’s bailer. Spring:
backbone. Summer: chief’s fishing line.
Autumn: Kawelo’s kite.
plan: **hard cut (no transition)** from 13: same frame, wide chart → north disc; E09; label as page 13
notes: EN48 p14 長圖轉北盤1＝鏡頭07開始 — 2 s — Four spokes, four seasons Winter: Makaliʻi’s bailer. Spring: backbone. Summer: chief’s fishing line. Autumn: Kawelo’s kite.

name: 鏡頭07結束＝鏡頭08開始
headline: Four spokes, four seasons
body:
Winter: Makaliʻi’s bailer. Spring:
backbone. Summer: chief’s fishing line.
Autumn: Kawelo’s kite.
plan: E09; disc labels Makaliʻi 的舀水杓／脊椎骨／酋長的釣線／Kawelo 的風箏 → Makaliʻi’s bailer／the backbone／the chief’s fishing line／Kawelo’s kite (labels keep the full names); then straight to 17 (page 16, the pointer stars, removed)
notes: EN48 p15 鏡頭07結束＝鏡頭08開始 — 6 s — Four spokes, four seasons Winter: Makaliʻi’s bailer. Spring: backbone. Summer: chief’s fishing line. Autumn: Kawelo’s kite.

name: 北盤轉長圖1-下移＝鏡頭09開始
headline: Are we there yet?
body:
Sail north for home — Hōkūleʻa climbs
higher each night.
plan: E11; label 南十字 → Southern Cross
notes: EN48 p19 北盤轉長圖1-下移＝鏡頭09開始 — 4 s — Are we there yet? Sail north for home — Hōkūleʻa climbs higher each night.

headline: Measuring Hawaiʻi’s latitude
plan: latitude diagram, English (`_概念圖/en/C-A09-02_緯度尺_天頂星層_透明.png`); E12 headline only
notes: EN48 p20 鏡頭09-概念圖1 — 4 s — Measuring Hawaiʻi’s latitude

name: 鏡頭13開始
headline: Winter’s line: Makaliʻi’s bailer
body:
From Capella to Sirius, it scoops up
Orion and the Pleiades as it rises.
plan: E13; labels 五車二／北河二／北河三／南河三／天狼星／參宿三／獵戶座 → Capella／Castor／Pollux／Procyon／Sirius／Mintaka／Orion (Hawaiian names stay)
notes: EN48 p30 鏡頭13開始 — 7 s — Winter’s line: Makaliʻi’s bailer From Capella to Sirius, it scoops up Orion and the Pleiades as it rises.

name: 鏡頭13結束＝鏡頭14開始
headline: Makahiki: the new-year season
body:
Each November, Makaliʻi (the Pleiades)
rises at sunset — four months for the
harvest god Lono.
plan: E14; **delete the two Siberian labels** (西伯利亞：鴨巢／打穀者; that episode is not in the English story); 昴宿星團／參宿三／獵戶座 → the Pleiades／Mintaka／Orion
notes: EN48 p31 鏡頭13結束＝鏡頭14開始 — 7 s — Makahiki: the new-year season Each November, Makaliʻi (the Pleiades) rises at sunset — four months for the harvest god Lono.

name: 鏡頭14結束
headline: Look up in January
body:
Around 20:00 (Northern Hemisphere), the
Pleiades stand high in the south.
plan: E15; labels 五車二／昴宿星團 → Capella／the Pleiades; then straight to 40 (pages 33–39, the turning disc and the Taipei-tonight horizon, removed)
notes: EN48 p32 鏡頭14結束 — 5 s — Look up in January Around 20:00 (Northern Hemisphere), the Pleiades stand high in the south.
